import re
import unicodedata


def slugify(text):
    # Decompose accented characters (NFKD) and drop the combining marks,
    # so "é" -> "e", "ü" -> "u", etc.
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
    ascii_text = "".join(c for c in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(c))
    ascii_text = ascii_text.lower()
    # Every run of characters other than a-z and 0-9 becomes one hyphen.
    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ascii_text)
    # No leading or trailing hyphens; empty string if nothing remains.
    return slug.strip("-")

# Release Checklist

Work through these steps in order. Do not skip steps.

## 1. Before you start

- [ ] Confirm the release scope: all intended changes are merged to the release branch.
- [ ] Confirm `main` (or the release branch) is green in CI.
- [ ] Working tree is clean: `git status` shows nothing to commit.

## 2. Version bump

- [ ] Decide the new version number using semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH).
- [ ] Update the version in the project's version source (e.g., the `VERSION` file or the version field in the package manifest).
- [ ] Make sure every other place that records the version is updated.
- [ ] Commit the bump: `git commit -am "Bump version to X.Y.Z"`.

## 3. Quality checks

- [ ] Run the test suite and confirm it passes.
- [ ] Run the linter in strict mode and confirm zero errors (e.g., `python lint.py --strict`).
- [ ] Build the artifacts and confirm the build succeeds.
- [ ] Smoke-test the built artifact on a clean environment.

## 4. Changelog and docs

- [ ] Update the changelog with the user-facing changes for this release.
- [ ] Update any docs or upgrade notes affected by the release.

## 5. Tag and publish

- [ ] Create an annotated git tag in the form `vX.Y.Z`: `git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "Release vX.Y.Z"`.
- [ ] Push the commit and tag: `git push origin <branch> && git push origin vX.Y.Z`.
- [ ] Publish the artifacts to the package registry or distribution channel.
- [ ] Verify the published artifact installs and runs from the registry.

## 6. Announce

- [ ] Post about the release in the #releases channel, including the version, a link to the changelog, and any required upgrade actions.

## 7. After the release

- [ ] Confirm the release notes and tag are visible in the repository.
- [ ] Open tracking issues for any follow-up work or regressions found.
- [ ] Reset the release branch or start the next development cycle as your process requires.

- [ ] Smoke tests pass against a staging environment

- [ ] Spot-check of critical user flows in production
- [ ] Customer-facing status updated if applicable

- [ ] Data corruption or loss is suspected
- [ ] A critical user flow is broken with no quick fix

- [ ] Milestone closed and remaining issues moved to the next release
- [ ] Release retrospective scheduled or notes captured
- [ ] Any hotfix branches or temporary flags cleaned up
- [ ] Release owner posted completion notice to the team

# Incident 2026-09-14: checkout latency

Status: resolved. Severity: SEV2. Duration: 14:05 to 15:40 UTC (95 minutes).

## Timeline

- 14:05 Alerts fired: p95 latency of POST /checkout rose from 300 ms to 9 s.
- 14:20 On-call (Ravi) rolled back the 13:50 deploy of the cart service. No change in latency.
- 14:48 The slow-query log showed full scans of the orders table.
- 15:10 Found that migration 0042 (applied at 13:45) rebuilt the orders table and did not recreate the index on orders.customer_id.
- 15:25 Index created with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.
- 15:40 Latency back to normal.

## Cause

Migration 0042 rebuilt the orders table to change a column type. The script copied the rows but did not recreate the index on orders.customer_id, so every customer lookup scanned about 12 million rows.

## Fix

Re-created the index with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which does not lock the table.

## Follow-ups

- Add a CI check that compares the index list before and after each migration (owner: Mei).
- The cart service deploy was unrelated to the incident and has been re-applied.

# Incident 2026-09-14: checkout latency

Status: resolved. Severity: SEV2. Duration: 14:05 to 15:40 UTC (95 minutes).

## Timeline

- 14:05 Alerts fired: p95 latency of POST /checkout rose from 300 ms to 9 s.
- 14:20 On-call (Ravi) rolled back the 13:50 deploy of the cart service. No change in latency.
- 14:48 The slow-query log showed full scans of the orders table.
- 15:10 Found that migration 0042 (applied at 13:45) rebuilt the orders table and did not recreate the index on orders.customer_id.
- 15:25 Index created with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.
- 15:40 Latency back to normal.

## Cause

Migration 0042 rebuilt the orders table to change a column type. The script copied the rows but did not recreate the index on orders.customer_id, so every customer lookup scanned about 12 million rows.

## Fix

Re-created the index with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which does not lock the table.

## Follow-ups

- Add a CI check that compares the index list before and after each migration (owner: Mei).
- The cart service deploy was unrelated to the incident and has been re-applied.

# Incident 2026-09-14: checkout latency

Status: resolved. Severity: SEV2. Duration: 14:05 to 15:40 UTC (95 minutes).

## Timeline

- 14:05 Alerts fired: p95 latency of POST /checkout rose from 300 ms to 9 s.
- 14:20 On-call (Ravi) rolled back the 13:50 deploy of the cart service. No change in latency.
- 14:48 The slow-query log showed full scans of the orders table.
- 15:10 Found that migration 0042 (applied at 13:45) rebuilt the orders table and did not recreate the index on orders.customer_id.
- 15:25 Index created with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.
- 15:40 Latency back to normal.

## Cause

Migration 0042 rebuilt the orders table to change a column type. The script copied the rows but did not recreate the index on orders.customer_id, so every customer lookup scanned about 12 million rows.

## Fix

Re-created the index with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which does not lock the table.

## Follow-ups

- Add a CI check that compares the index list before and after each migration (owner: Mei).
- The cart service deploy was unrelated to the incident and has been re-applied.
